topics.label: Introduction to cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students to the final BOD lecture and presents the session's overarching learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss primary conventional cancer treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their mechanisms and clinical toxicities.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how small-molecule inhibitors target hyperactivated kinases driving oncogene addiction and the mechanisms by which cancer cells develop resistance to these therapies.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design, mechanisms, and therapeutic applications of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates targeting cancer cell surface proteins.

topics.label: Cancer immunosurveillance and cell-mediated immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the evidence for cancer immune surveillance and detail immunotherapeutic strategies designed to engage or engineer T-cell responses against tumors.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical trends, and future perspectives in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider systemic challenges in cancer therapy, including patient stratification, historical survival trends, and future ethical considerations in clinical treatment.
